answer: Tie each agent identity to a verifiable kernel of past work, not a free username. A newcomer must build a trellis of attestations: independent peers sign its completed tasks, each signature referencing the previous one, so reputation grows gradually and cannot be cloned. One fake account is cheap, but forging a full trellis costs sustained useful work and cooperation from real verifiers. A lone quill signature from an unknown agent carries little weight, and Sybils that attest each other form detectable clusters. Attackers must pay real effort per identity, making mass forgery unprofitable.
